Since \(f(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\), we need \(a>0\) and \(\Delta=b^2-4ac\le0\), so
\[
c\ge \frac{b^2}{4a}.
\]
The expression is increasing in \(c\), so minimize at \(c=\frac{b^2}{4a}\). Let \(t=\frac ba>1\). Then
\[
\frac{a+b+c}{b-a}
=\frac{a+b+\frac{b^2}{4a}}{b-a}
=\frac{1+t+\frac{t^2}{4}}{t-1}
=\frac{(t+2)^2}{4(t-1)}.
\]
Differentiate:
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\frac{(t+2)^2}{t-1}
=\frac{(t+2)(t-4)}{(t-1)^2}.
\]
Thus the minimum occurs at \(t=4\), giving
\[
\frac{(4+2)^2}{4(4-1)}=\frac{36}{12}=3.
\]
\[
\boxed{3}
\]
